content: The right auricular appendix, also referred to as the right auricula or right auricle, is a small, conical, muscular pouch that is anatomically attached to the right atrium of the heart. Its edges are characterized by a dentated or notched appearance. This structure extends forward and slightly to the left from the upper and anterior portion of the sinus, overlapping the root of the aorta. The inner surface of the right auricle, along with the body of the right atrium, is lined with pectinate muscles. These muscles form a complex network of ridges and grooves, giving the surface a trabeculated appearance. Historically, the term right auricle was often used interchangeably to describe what is now more accurately referred to as the right atrium in older medical literature.
